prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: extract-images
Deck beneath it: Red rectangles drawn on the scan say cut here; blue ones say erase this — every picture is cut free, cleaned, and logged.

Hero: a paper-cutter's workbench fills the middle of the page. A large scanned book page lies on it, and on that page two engravings are each ringed by a hand-drawn red rectangle, loose and human, not ruler-straight. Inside one engraving a smaller blue rectangle covers an intruding printed caption. Above the bench, a slender craft knife on an articulated arm follows the red line, and the first picture is shown half-lifted from the page, its cut edge crisp. A note at the knife: the knife follows the red line, then trims the red ink itself off the finished edge.

To the right of the bench, the lifted picture in three small states arranged downward:
- first, freshly cut, the blue rectangle still on it;
- second, the blue region painted out white, a fine brush resting beside it, captioned: whatever the blue box covered is painted away;
- third, the cleaned picture turned a quarter-turn, with a small curved arrow, captioned: a page marked rotate is stood upright before filing.

The finished pictures descend into a filing tray at the lower right, each in a paper sleeve tabbed with its name — p041-1, p041-2, p052-1 — and beside the tray lies an open ledger labeled manifest.yaml, its columns showing each picture's page, order, and size, with small tick-marks in columns headed blue, sky, and turned. A note at the ledger: every cut is logged; the composing stage later deals these pictures back to their pages by this ledger.

One quiet inset at the lower left: a magnified corner of the scan where a faint red speck and a tiny stray mark sit untouched beside a proper red rectangle, captioned — only deliberate rectangles count; specks and solid smears are passed over.

The red of the drawn rectangles is its own quiet second accent; one warm accent colour follows the cut pictures to their tray, and blue appears only as the two erase boxes. Bench, page, and ledger stay in ink.
